advances: Three actual planar integer fibers with equal-area triangular endpoints and an arbitrary containing middle body.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The middle inclusion gives $y$ in the actual middle fiber. It also makes these the only integer fibers of the lifted convex hull, since at base zero any endpoint contribution combines the endpoints with equal weights and can be absorbed in $K$. By the shear in the directional profile theorem the two endpoint centroids and $y$ are zero in the new fiber coordinates. For any nonzero continuous normal normalize its length and put the associated coordinate along the first axis. A common scaling reduces the areas to one and an inverse rescaling of the two coordinates makes the first axial width one while preserving the areas. Each normalized triangle has a two-piece affine section length, meeting at the middle vertex height, with the degenerate one-sided case for a facet support. Its area one fixes the height and the mean of its vertex heights fixes the axial centering. Thus the two profiles are exactly the tents used in the all-tent whole-cap bound. The sharp directional profile theorem identifies the least middle cap compatible with the profiles as the cap of the averaged symmetric kites. The all-tent bound then pays $4/3$ in those units for the given tilt. Undoing the scaling gives $4v/3$. Pure integer through-$y$ caps capture $K$ and one endpoint, of total area at least $2v$ by planar Brunn–Minkowski and midpoint inclusion. A general containing cap contains its through-point translate.

For the other candidate take density identically one on $K$ in accepted fact 6769574fc1bd9f8d. It gives depth at least $4k/9$ from the middle fiber alone. The ratio $\max\{4v/3,4k/9\}/(k+2v)$ decreases to $4/15$ for $k/v\le3$ and increases from $4/15$ for $k/v\ge3$, by evaluating the appropriate branch. The two comparisons with $(k+v)/3$ are respectively $4v\ge k+v$ and $4k\ge3(k+v)$. When all fibers equal one triangle, a facet-parallel vertex cap through its centroid has area $4v/9$ by triangular similarity, and taking that same halfplane in all fibers gives equality at $y$.

[Brunn–Minkowski, Gardner, The Brunn–Minkowski Inequality, Theorem 4.1](https://sites.stat.washington.edu/jaw/COURSES/520s/523/HO.523.20/Gardner.BullAMS.02.pdf).

statement: Let $A,B$ be planar triangles of equal positive area $v$, let $K$ be a planar convex body containing $(A+B)/2$, and write $k=|K|$. In the actual three fibers $A,K,B$ at bases $-1,0,1$ with summed area measure, every closed ambient halfspace containing $y=(0,(g_A+g_B)/2)$ has raw mass at least $4v/3$. Equality holds at this point when $A=B=K$ is a triangle. The maximum raw depth is at least $\max\{4v/3,4k/9\}$, so the normalized maximum is at least $4/15$. The prescribed $y$ pays $(k+v)/3$ when $v\le k\le3v$, and the middle centroid pays it when $k\ge3v$.
title: Equal-area triangle endpoints pay at their centroid midpoint
